title: Swift Algorithms: windows & adjacentPairs
hints: A window is a slice `self[start..<end]`; slide both indices forward together.
Use `index(_:offsetBy:)` for the first end, then `formIndex(after:)` on both each step.
jsBridge: `windows(ofCount:)` gives sliding windows as slices without copying, and `adjacentPairs()` gives neighbours. JS would loop with indices and `slice`, which copies every window.

compass.q: JS `slice` for each window copies k elements. What does returning `SubSequence` avoid?
Sliding-window sum recomputed per window vs incrementally: O(nk) vs O(n).
What does `windows(ofCount: 0)` or a count larger than the collection return?
Moving averages for charts (heart rate, stock price) use windows. Where would you compute them?
